hypothesis: Kevin's benchmark table reads settle 669 (Pi 688, rust AHEAD ~3%) from the r2 campaign, but the settle-hold lane's paired ABBA at the current base (b1c6b7a0c) reverses it: rust p50 755.0 vs pi 683.8, 0/14 blocks rust-faster, p=0.00012, and the healthy-window rust floor (732.8) exceeds pi's max (691.3). Two questions: (1) does the reversal survive a dedicated confirmation leg, and is it honest against the r2 anchor (rust 668.9 vs pi 688.3 at e75f59efc6) — the same-sha framing must be corrected: the anchor sits 25 commits and one VM away; (2) what class is the daemon-init bind-span (~39ms in the earlier ledger, per the lazyinit lane's LEG-INLINE vs LEG-PREWARMED framing): Supervisor::new config persist + telemetry install + settings/catalog chain before bind_transport, and which share is product work vs host write-regime.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY (no product change). Four legs on one quiet 16c/32GB Prime VM (hillclimb-perf-settlehold, sandbox u5nxl6eddrafmr7cbe1viyui, ubuntu:22.04, rustup 1.98.1, bench harness at /root/bench-harness, lane arms staged release-pipeline shape): LEG1+CONFIRM the settle-hold paired ABBA (compare.msg_send mock-routed, PTY driver, per-trial fresh launch, 14 blocks of A,B,B,A = 28 trials/arm; arm A = rust b1c6b7a0c payload sha a07f3c41 via the lane launcher, arm B = pi 0.99.1@d86654ab cli.js sha e79626f2; blocks b1-b11 07:00-07:17Z, blocks b12-b14 confirmation 07:25-07:30Z); LEG2 the daemon-init decompose (bench-identical daemon launch on fresh trial dirs: 24 clean + 5 drop_caches=3 cold legs with a 1ms socket-stat bind grid, 2ms /proc sighting grid, /proc start-tick + sock mtime_ns cross-checks, daemon CPU ticks at bind, connect + hello wire view, 30-round grid-floor control, spin calibration; plus 6 strace legs with the ptrace-inflation honesty — traced spans never reported clean); LEG3 the settle-tail decompose attempt (protocol-identical + per-chunk PTY ledger replay, rust n=6, pi n=4) — HONEST NEGATIVE: the needle detector never matched, no tail numbers; LEG4 the sha-isolate ABBA (the discriminator the discrepancy demanded): the r2 pin's EXACT BYTES (payload sha 0ba7c9b6e6..., '0.9.8-continuous.e75f59efc6', staged verbatim from the r2 staging tree) registered as a second bench product rust-e75 (settle walk OK, kernel venv warmed from its own payload), ABBA'd against the lane pin in 4 blocks of (e75, b1c6, b1c6, e75) = 8 trials/arm, per-round versions.json sha pins verified for all 16 rounds. I/O advisory v1.0 regime probes at EVERY leg boundary (>=40 ISOLATED fresh+sync_all+rename @0.5s + >=20 repeat-fsync, host-relative, PHASE MODEL re-classification, NO-CEILING in-leg labels); PID-list zombie sweep before timing legs; noop PTY floor controls per round (56 rounds leg1, 16 rounds leg4); spin calibration pre/mid/post.
parity_notes: No product bytes changed anywhere. LEG4's rust-e75 arm is the r2 campaign pin's own payload staged verbatim (sha 0ba7c9b6e6277b6301605769240d133727d59dc1997890e333e54518ce5a88e5) as a second bench product — a measurement arm, not a product change; its kernel venv was warmed from its own payload (global/rust-e75/kernel-venv, bench.drivers.warm_kernels), the settle walk passed, and per-round versions.json pins every arm's binary sha. The pi arm is byte-identical to the r2 campaign's pi arm (0.99.1@d86654ab, cli.js e79626f2), which makes it the cross-campaign control. The strace legs used a syscall filter that omits link/linkat: the telemetry install's atomic create is inferred as O_EXCL+write+fsync+LINK+unlink (the unlink-after-fsync on a file that then reads back proves the link); disclosed as inference. The msg_send metric is kernel-venv-insensitive (the turn completes without kernel interaction; the venv warms the launch path), so the e75 arm's venv provenance does not touch the settle clock.

(3) THE BIND-SPAN CLASS ANSWER (gates the lazyinit lane's L1): the span is LEG-INLINE and IO-CLASS on every daemon-booting create path — TWO inline fresh-fsyncs on the fresh-agent-dir path (supervisor-config persist ~34-38ms + telemetry install-id ~31-34ms on this host class), ONE on the warm-agent-dir path (supervisor-config persist; the ~39ms ledger = this class), everything else ~5-7ms, binary-load only +3-10ms cold — so the lazyinit L1 (unsynced supervisor-config persist, TS parity at the writeFileAtomicSync call site) is the RIGHT CLASS and the right first cut, and the telemetry install-id fsync survives it as the fresh-path residual candidate (TS-parity check first); LEG-PREWARMED (binary prewarm) would only buy the ~2-5ms load share. The daemon is ready AT bind (bind->connect ~1ms, connect->hello ~0.7ms, hello 24/24). No PR from this lane (measurement-only); the drift-bisect follow-up is the actionable cut-path.
